9. Tool Registry
Le Registry est le cœur de D.3.
from collections.abc import Iterable

from .tool_definition import ToolDefinition
from ..exceptions import (
    ToolDisabledError,
    ToolNotFoundError,
)


class ToolRegistry:

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._tools: dict[str, ToolDefinition] = {}

    def register(self, tool: ToolDefinition) -> None:

        if tool.name in self._tools:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Tool already registered: {tool.name}"
            )

        self._tools[tool.name] = tool

    def unregister(self, name: str) -> None:
        self._tools.pop(name, None)

    def resolve(self, name: str) -> ToolDefinition:

        tool = self._tools.get(name)

        if tool is None:
            raise ToolNotFoundError(name)

        if not tool.enabled:
            raise ToolDisabledError(name)

        return tool

    def list(self) -> list[ToolDefinition]:
        return list(self._tools.values())

    def discover(
        self,
        capabilities: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    ) -> list[ToolDefinition]:

        if not capabilities:
            return self.list()

        required = set(capabilities)

        return [
            tool
            for tool in self._tools.values()
            if required.issubset(tool.capabilities)
            and tool.enabled
        ]

10. Dynamic Discovery
Le système doit pouvoir découvrir automatiquement les outils.
import importlib
import pkgutil


class ToolDiscovery:

    def __init__(self, registry: ToolRegistry):
        self.registry = registry

    def discover_package(self, package_name: str) -> None:

        package = importlib.import_module(package_name)

        for module_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(
            package.__path__
        ):
            module_name = (
                f"{package_name}.{module_info.name}"
            )

            importlib.import_module(module_name)
Mais l'import automatique seul n'est pas suffisant.
Chaque module doit exposer explicitement ses outils.

11. Decorator @tool
On peut rendre l'enregistrement extrêmement propre :
_TOOL_DEFINITIONS: list[ToolDefinition] = []


def tool(
    *,
    name: str,
    version: str,
    description: str,
    input_schema: dict,
    output_schema: dict,
    capabilities: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    permissions=frozenset(),
    risk_level=ToolRisk.LOW,
    timeout_seconds: int = 30,
    requires_sandbox: bool = True,
):
    def decorator(handler):

        definition = ToolDefinition(
            name=name,
            version=version,
            description=description,
            handler=handler,
            input_schema=input_schema,
            output_schema=output_schema,
            capabilities=capabilities,
            permissions=permissions,
            risk_level=risk_level,
            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
            requires_sandbox=requires_sandbox,
        )

        _TOOL_DEFINITIONS.append(definition)

        return handler

    return decorator

12. Exemple : filesystem.read
from pathlib import Path

from ..registry.decorator import tool
from ..tool_definition import PermissionLevel, ToolRisk


@tool(
    name="filesystem.read",
    version="1.0.0",
    description="Read a file from the workspace.",
    input_schema={
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "path": {
                "type": "string",
            },
        },
        "required": ["path"],
        "additionalProperties": False,
    },
    output_schema={
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "path": {"type": "string"},
            "content": {"type": "string"},
        },
        "required": ["path", "content"],
    },
    capabilities=frozenset({
        "filesystem",
        "filesystem.read",
    }),
    permissions=frozenset({
        PermissionLevel.READ,
    }),
    risk_level=ToolRisk.LOW,
)
async def filesystem_read(
    *,
    path: str,
    context: ToolContext,
) -> dict:

    await context.cancellation_token.check()

    target = Path(path)

    content = target.read_text(
        encoding="utf-8"
    )

    return {
        "path": str(target),
        "content": content,
    }
Mais cette version devra ensuite être renforcée par le Workspace Security Layer : le chemin fourni ne doit jamais permettre de sortir du workspace.

13. Tool Validator
Le validator doit contrôler les arguments avant exécution.
Je recommande jsonschema.
from jsonschema import ValidationError
from jsonschema import validate

from ..exceptions import ToolValidationError
from .tool_definition import ToolDefinition


class ToolValidator:

    def validate(
        self,
        tool: ToolDefinition,
        arguments: dict,
    ) -> None:

        try:
            validate(
                instance=arguments,
                schema=tool.input_schema,
            )

        except ValidationError as exc:
            raise ToolValidationError(
                f"Invalid arguments for {tool.name}: "
                f"{exc.message}"
            ) from exc
Le résultat doit être :
LLM arguments
      ↓
JSON schema
      ↓
VALID
      ↓
policy
et jamais :
LLM → Python function
directement.

14. Permission Engine
from ..exceptions import ToolPermissionDeniedError
from .tool_definition import ToolDefinition, PermissionLevel


class PermissionEngine:

    def check(
        self,
        *,
        tool: ToolDefinition,
        granted_permissions: set[PermissionLevel],
    ) -> None:

        required = set(tool.permissions)

        if not required.issubset(granted_permissions):

            missing = required - granted_permissions

            raise ToolPermissionDeniedError(
                f"Missing permissions: {missing}"
            )

15. Risk Engine
Le niveau de risque ne doit pas être uniquement celui enregistré dans PostgreSQL.
Le risque réel dépend également du contexte.
Par exemple :
filesystem.write
dans :
/home/project/src/foo.py
≠
/etc/passwd
Donc :
class RiskEngine:

    def calculate(
        self,
        tool: ToolDefinition,
        arguments: dict,
        context: ToolContext,
    ) -> float:

        score = {
            ToolRisk.LOW: 0.10,
            ToolRisk.MEDIUM: 0.40,
            ToolRisk.HIGH: 0.70,
            ToolRisk.CRITICAL: 0.95,
        }[tool.risk_level]

        return score
Puis D.3.1 pourra introduire :

CONTEXTUAL RISK

+
BLAST RADIUS

DYNAMIC RISK SCORE

16. Approval Engine
class ApprovalEngine:

    def requires_approval(
        self,
        *,
        tool: ToolDefinition,
        risk_score: float,
    ) -> bool:

        if tool.requires_approval:
            return True

        if risk_score >= 0.80:
            return True

        return False
Ce moteur doit ensuite créer :
execution.approval_requests
avant l'exécution.

18. Tool Executor
Voici le cœur opérationnel.
import asyncio
import time

from ..exceptions import ToolTimeoutError
from .tool_result import ToolResult
from .tool_context import ToolContext


class ToolExecutor:

    def __init__(
        self,
        registry,
        validator,
        permission_engine,
        risk_engine,
        approval_engine,
    ):
        self.registry = registry
        self.validator = validator
        self.permission_engine = permission_engine
        self.risk_engine = risk_engine
        self.approval_engine = approval_engine

    async def execute(
        self,
        *,
        tool_name: str,
        arguments: dict,
        context: ToolContext,
        granted_permissions: set,
    ) -> ToolResult:

        started = time.perf_counter()

        tool = self.registry.resolve(tool_name)

        self.validator.validate(
            tool,
            arguments,
        )

        self.permission_engine.check(
            tool=tool,
            granted_permissions=granted_permissions,
        )

        risk_score = self.risk_engine.calculate(
            tool,
            arguments,
            context,
        )

        if self.approval_engine.requires_approval(
            tool=tool,
            risk_score=risk_score,
        ):
            raise ToolApprovalRequiredError(
                f"Approval required for {tool.name}"
            )

        try:

            result = await asyncio.wait_for(
                tool.handler(
                    **arguments,
                    context=context,
                ),
                timeout=tool.timeout_seconds,
            )

            duration = int(
                (time.perf_counter() - started)
                * 1000
            )

            return ToolResult(
                success=True,
                data=result,
                duration_ms=duration,
                metadata={
                    "tool": tool.name,
                    "version": tool.version,
                    "risk_score": risk_score,
                },
            )

        except asyncio.TimeoutError as exc:

            raise ToolTimeoutError(
                f"Tool timed out: {tool.name}"
            ) from exc

19. Mais il manque une pièce essentielle : ExecutionService
Le ToolExecutor ne doit pas être responsable de toute la persistance.
Architecture :
Agent
  ↓
ExecutionService
  ↓
ToolExecutor
  ↓
Tool
Le ExecutionService gère :
execution.executions
execution.execution_steps
execution.execution_attempts
execution.tool_calls
execution.execution_events
execution.observations
execution.resource_usage

20. Execution Service
class ExecutionService:

    def __init__(
        self,
        tool_executor,
        audit_service,
    ):
        self.tool_executor = tool_executor
        self.audit_service = audit_service

    async def execute_tool(
        self,
        *,
        tool_name: str,
        arguments: dict,
        context,
        permissions: set,
    ):

        await self.audit_service.tool_call_started(
            context=context,
            tool_name=tool_name,
            arguments=arguments,
        )

        try:

            result = await self.tool_executor.execute(
                tool_name=tool_name,
                arguments=arguments,
                context=context,
                granted_permissions=permissions,
            )

            await self.audit_service.tool_call_completed(
                context=context,
                tool_name=tool_name,
                result=result,
            )

            return result

        except Exception as exc:

            await self.audit_service.tool_call_failed(
                context=context,
                tool_name=tool_name,
                error=exc,
            )

            raise

25. ToolLoader
class ToolLoader:

    def __init__(self, registry):
        self.registry = registry

    async def load_from_database(
        self,
        session,
        tenant_id,
    ):

        rows = await self._load_tools(
            session,
            tenant_id,
        )

        for row in rows:

            handler = self._resolve_handler(
                row.implementation
            )

            definition = ToolDefinition(
                name=row.name,
                version=row.version,
                description=row.description,
                handler=handler,
                input_schema=row.input_schema,
                output_schema=row.output_schema,
                capabilities=frozenset(
                    row.capabilities
                ),
                permissions=frozenset(
                    row.permissions
                ),
                risk_level=row.risk_level,
                timeout_seconds=row.timeout_seconds,
                enabled=row.enabled,
            )

            self.registry.register(
                definition
            )

26. Résolution de l'implementation
La colonne DB peut contenir :
yahria.execution.adapters.filesystem:filesystem_read
Le loader utilise :
import importlib


def resolve_handler(path: str):

    module_name, function_name = path.split(":")

    module = importlib.import_module(
        module_name
    )

    return getattr(
        module,
        function_name,
    )
Mais pour la sécurité industrielle, je recommande une allowlist d'implémentations.
Ne jamais permettre :
DB → importlib → n'importe quel chemin arbitraire

27. Secure Tool Loader
ALLOWED_TOOL_MODULES = {
    "yahria.execution.adapters.filesystem",
    "yahria.execution.adapters.terminal",
    "yahria.execution.adapters.git",
    "yahria.execution.adapters.search",
    "yahria.execution.adapters.tests",
    "yahria.execution.adapters.browser",
}
Puis :
def resolve_handler(path: str):

    module_name, function_name = path.split(":", 1)

    if module_name not in ALLOWED_TOOL_MODULES:
        raise PermissionError(
            f"Unauthorized tool module: {module_name}"
        )

    module = importlib.import_module(module_name)

    handler = getattr(module, function_name)

    if not callable(handler):
        raise TypeError(
            f"Tool handler is not callable: {path}"
        )

    return handler

Je recommande d'ajouter au niveau runtime :

Ces données pourront alimenter plus tard le Meta Intelligence Layer de YAHRIA.

31. Retry Engine
Tous les outils ne doivent pas être automatiquement rejoués.
filesystem.read     → retry possible
search.code         → retry possible
terminal.execute    → conditionnel
filesystem.write    → idempotence nécessaire
git.commit          → généralement non
git.push             → non automatique
database.migrate     → approval
production.deploy    → approval obligatoire
Donc :
class RetryPolicy:

    def can_retry(
        self,
        *,
        tool,
        error,
    ) -> bool:

        if tool.max_retries <= 0:
            return False

        return error.retryable

32. Idempotence
D.3 doit déjà préparer l'idempotence :
tenant_id
+
execution_id
+
tool_name
+
idempotency_key
permettent d'éviter :
Agent
  ↓
filesystem.write
  ↓
timeout réseau
  ↓
Agent croit que ça a échoué
  ↓
retry
  ↓
double opération
La table tool_calls doit idéalement recevoir :
idempotency_key
avec une contrainte unique adaptée au tenant.

33. Tool Call Lifecycle
Je recommande :
CREATED
   ↓
VALIDATING
   ↓
AUTHORIZED
   ↓
APPROVAL_PENDING
   ↓
APPROVED
   ↓

   ↓

   ↓

ou :

Donc il serait pertinent d'ajouter à D.2 un enum :
class ToolCallStatus(StrEnum):
    CREATED = "created"
    VALIDATING = "validating"
    AUTHORIZED = "authorized"
    APPROVAL_PENDING = "approval_pending"
    APPROVED = "approved"
    DENIED = "denied"
    STARTING = "starting"
    RUNNING = "running"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    TIMEOUT = "timeout"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

37. Point essentiel : Terminal Security
terminal.execute est l'outil le plus dangereux.
Il ne faut jamais faire :
subprocess.run(command, shell=True)
avec une commande directement produite par le LLM.
YAHRIA doit faire :
LLM command
      ↓
Command Parser
      ↓
Command Policy
      ↓
Risk Engine
      ↓
Allowlist / Denylist
      ↓
Sandbox
      ↓
Resource Limits
      ↓
Execution
Exemple :
pytest
ruff
mypy
npm test
npm run build
peuvent être autorisés.
Mais :
rm -rf /
curl ... | bash
chmod 777 ...
dd if=/dev/...
shutdown
mkfs
doivent être bloqués ou soumis à une politique critique.

38. Architecture Terminal
terminal.execute
       │
       ▼
CommandParser
       │
       ▼
CommandPolicy
       │
       ├── allowed
       ├── denied
       └── approval
       │
       ▼
Sandbox
       │
       ▼
ResourceManager
       │
       ▼
ProcessRunner
       │
       ├── stdout
       ├── stderr
       ├── exit_code
       └── resource_usage
Cette partie sera particulièrement importante dans D.4 Sandbox Engine.

39. Tool Registry API
L'API interne pourra exposer :
GET    /api/v1/execution/tools
GET    /api/v1/execution/tools/{name}
GET    /api/v1/execution/tools/{name}/versions

POST   /api/v1/execution/tools/resolve
POST   /api/v1/execution/tool-calls
GET    /api/v1/execution/tool-calls/{id}

POST   /api/v1/execution/tool-calls/{id}/approve
POST   /api/v1/execution/tool-calls/{id}/deny
POST   /api/v1/execution/tool-calls/{id}/cancel
Mais l'Agent Runtime doit idéalement utiliser un service Python interne, pas HTTP, lorsqu'il fonctionne dans le même processus.

41. Ce que D.3 verrouille
À la fin de V2.2.2-D.3, YAHRIA dispose d'un véritable :
Tool Registry
    • découverte dynamique ; 
    • enregistrement ; 
    • versioning ; 
    • résolution ; 
    • capability matching. 
Tool Validation
    • JSON Schema ; 
    • validation stricte ; 
    • output normalization. 
Policy Engine
    • permissions ; 
    • RBAC/ABAC ; 
    • risque ; 
    • approbation. 
Tool Runtime
    • contexte isolé ; 
    • timeout ; 
    • cancellation ; 
    • retries ; 
    • idempotence ; 
    • métriques. 
Security
    • sandbox obligatoire ; 
    • path isolation ; 
    • command policy ; 
    • réseau contrôlé ; 
    • secrets indirects ; 
    • audit. 
Observability
    • tool calls ; 
    • événements ; 
    • observations ; 
    • erreurs ; 
    • resource usage ; 
    • latence ; 
    • fiabilité.

La prochaine production technique que je recommande est donc V2.2.2-D.3.1 : Tool Registry Engine — implémentation production complète, avec les fichiers Python réels, les modèles SQLAlchemy correspondant exactement aux tables D.2, ToolRegistry, ToolLoader, ToolValidator, PermissionEngine, RiskEngine, ApprovalEngine, ToolExecutor, les adapters filesystem/terminal/git/search/test, les tests Pytest et les seeds PostgreSQL des outils. Cela permettra ensuite d'attaquer D.4 Sandbox Engine sans devoir refaire l'interface d'exécution.
donc V2.2.2-D.3.1 : 
Exactement.
V2.2.2-D.3.1 — TOOL REGISTRY ENGINE · PRODUCTION IMPLEMENTATION
Je le définirais comme le livrable technique complet qui transforme D.3 d'une architecture conceptuelle en un composant réellement intégrable dans YAHRIA.

4. models/base.py
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Annotated
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import DateTime, func
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID as PGUUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


UUIDPK = Annotated[
    UUID,
    mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    ),
]


class TimestampMixin:

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        server_default=func.now(),
        nullable=False,
    )

    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        server_default=func.now(),
        onupdate=func.now(),
        nullable=False,
    )

5. models/tool.py
C'est la table principale :
execution.tools
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import (
    Boolean,
    CheckConstraint,
    ForeignKey,
    Index,
    Integer,
    String,
    Text,
    UniqueConstraint,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB, UUID as PGUUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

from .base import Base, TimestampMixin, UUIDPK
from ..domain.enums import PermissionLevel, ToolRisk


class Tool(Base, TimestampMixin):
    __tablename__ = "tools"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id",
            "name",
            name="uq_execution_tools_tenant_name",
        ),
        CheckConstraint(
            "timeout_seconds > 0",
            name="ck_execution_tools_timeout_positive",
        ),
        Index(
            "ix_execution_tools_tenant_enabled",
            "tenant_id",
            "enabled",
        ),
        Index(
            "ix_execution_tools_tenant_risk",
            "tenant_id",
            "risk_level",
        ),
        {"schema": "execution"},
    )

    id: Mapped[UUIDPK]

    tenant_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    risk_level: Mapped[ToolRisk] = mapped_column(
        nullable=False,
    )

    permission_level: Mapped[PermissionLevel] = mapped_column(
        nullable=False,
    )

    enabled: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=True,
        server_default="true",
    )

    input_schema: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
        server_default="{}",
    )

    output_schema: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
        server_default="{}",
    )

    timeout_seconds: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        Integer,
        nullable=False,
        default=30,
        server_default="30",
    )

    metadata_: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = mapped_column(
        "metadata",
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
        server_default="{}",
    )

    versions: Mapped[list["ToolVersion"]] = relationship(
        back_populates="tool",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        lazy="selectin",
    )

    capabilities: Mapped[list["ToolCapability"]] = relationship(
        back_populates="tool",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        lazy="selectin",
    )

    permissions: Mapped[list["ToolPermission"]] = relationship(
        back_populates="tool",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        lazy="selectin",
    )

    calls: Mapped[list["ToolCall"]] = relationship(
        back_populates="tool",
        lazy="noload",
    )

6. PostgreSQL Enum mapping
Pour garder les enums PostgreSQL de D.2, il est préférable de déclarer explicitement les types dans le modèle.
Le modèle Tool devient donc :
from sqlalchemy import Enum as SAEnum

risk_level: Mapped[ToolRisk] = mapped_column(
    SAEnum(
        ToolRisk,
        name="tool_risk",
        schema="execution",
        native_enum=True,
        create_type=False,
    ),
    nullable=False,
)

permission_level: Mapped[PermissionLevel] = mapped_column(
    SAEnum(
        PermissionLevel,
        name="permission_level",
        schema="execution",
        native_enum=True,
        create_type=False,
    ),
    nullable=False,
)
Important : create_type=False est volontaire.
Les enums sont créés par la migration D.2 :
002_execution_enums.py
D.3.1-A ne doit pas tenter de recréer les types PostgreSQL.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import (
    Boolean,
    CheckConstraint,
    ForeignKey,
    Index,
    String,
    Text,
    UniqueConstraint,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB, UUID as PGUUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

from .base import Base, TimestampMixin, UUIDPK
from ..domain.enums import ToolImplementationType, ToolVersionStatus
from sqlalchemy import Enum as SAEnum


class ToolVersion(Base, TimestampMixin):
    __tablename__ = "tool_versions"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(
            "tool_id",
            "version",
            name="uq_execution_tool_versions_tool_version",
        ),
        Index(
            "ix_execution_tool_versions_tool_status",
            "tool_id",
            "status",
        ),
        CheckConstraint(
            "version <> ''",
            name="ck_execution_tool_versions_version_not_empty",
        ),
        {"schema": "execution"},
    )

    id: Mapped[UUIDPK]

    tool_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey(
            "execution.tools.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    version: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    implementation: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    implementation_type: Mapped[ToolImplementationType] = mapped_column(
        SAEnum(
            ToolImplementationType,
            name="tool_implementation_type",
            schema="execution",
            native_enum=True,
            create_type=False,
        ),
        nullable=False,
        default=ToolImplementationType.PYTHON,
    )

    checksum: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(128),
        nullable=True,
    )

    status: Mapped[ToolVersionStatus] = mapped_column(
        SAEnum(
            ToolVersionStatus,
            name="tool_version_status",
            schema="execution",
            native_enum=True,
            create_type=False,
        ),
        nullable=False,
        default=ToolVersionStatus.INACTIVE,
    )

    enabled: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=True,
        server_default="true",
    )

    metadata_: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = mapped_column(
        "metadata",
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
        server_default="{}",
    )

    tool: Mapped["Tool"] = relationship(
        back_populates="versions",
    )

    calls: Mapped[list["ToolCall"]] = relationship(
        back_populates="tool_version",
        lazy="noload",
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import (
    CheckConstraint,

    Index,
    Integer,
    String,
    UniqueConstraint,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB, UUID as PGUUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

from .base import Base, TimestampMixin, UUIDPK

from ..domain.enums import (
    ApprovalStatus,
    ToolCallStatus,
    ToolRisk,
)

from sqlalchemy import Enum as SAEnum


class ToolCall(Base, TimestampMixin):
    __tablename__ = "tool_calls"

    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id",
            "idempotency_key",
            name="uq_execution_tool_calls_idempotency",
        ),
        CheckConstraint(
            "duration_ms IS NULL OR duration_ms >= 0",
            name="ck_execution_tool_calls_duration_nonnegative",
        ),
        Index(
            "ix_execution_tool_calls_execution",
            "execution_id",
        ),
        Index(
            "ix_execution_tool_calls_agent",
            "agent_run_id",
        ),
        Index(
            "ix_execution_tool_calls_status",
            "tenant_id",
            "status",
        ),
        Index(
            "ix_execution_tool_calls_tool",
            "tool_id",
        ),
        {"schema": "execution"},
    )

    id: Mapped[UUIDPK]

    tenant_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,

    execution_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(

    error_code: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=True,
    )

    error_message: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String,
        nullable=True,
    )

    started_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=True,
    )

    finished_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=True,
    )

    duration_ms: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(
        Integer,
        nullable=True,
    )

    metadata_: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = mapped_column(
        "metadata",
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
        server_default="{}",
    )

    tool: Mapped["Tool"] = relationship(
        back_populates="calls",
    )

    tool_version: Mapped["ToolVersion | None"] = relationship(
        back_populates="calls",
    )

11. Point important sur tool_calls
Je recommande cette évolution par rapport au D.2 initial :
tenant_id
+
idempotency_key
avec :
UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key)
Cela permet :
retry
  ↓
même idempotency_key
  ↓
détection
  ↓
pas de double exécution
Mais une valeur NULL reste autorisée pour les opérations qui n'ont pas besoin d'idempotence.

14. tool_repository.py
from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from ..models.tool import Tool


class ToolRepository:

    def __init__(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession,
    ) -> None:
        self.session = session

    async def get(
        self,
        tool_id: UUID,
    ) -> Tool | None:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(Tool)
            .where(Tool.id == tool_id)
        )

        return result.scalar_one_or_none()

    async def get_by_name(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: UUID,
        name: str,
    ) -> Tool | None:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(Tool)
            .where(
                Tool.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                Tool.name == name,
            )
        )

        return result.scalar_one_or_none()

    async def list_enabled(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: UUID,
    ) -> list[Tool]:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(Tool)
            .where(
                Tool.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                Tool.enabled.is_(True),
            )
            .order_by(Tool.name)
        )

        return list(result.scalars().all())

    async def create(
        self,
        tool: Tool,
    ) -> Tool:

        self.session.add(tool)

        await self.session.flush()

        return tool

    async def save(
        self,
        tool: Tool,
    ) -> Tool:

        self.session.add(tool)

        await self.session.flush()

        return tool

    async def delete(
        self,
        tool: Tool,
    ) -> None:

        await self.session.delete(tool)

        await self.session.flush()

from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from ..models.tool_version import ToolVersion
from ..domain.enums import ToolVersionStatus


class ToolVersionRepository:

    def __init__(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession,
    ) -> None:
        self.session = session

    async def get(
        self,
        version_id: UUID,
    ) -> ToolVersion | None:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(ToolVersion)
            .where(ToolVersion.id == version_id)
        )

        return result.scalar_one_or_none()

    async def get_version(
        self,
        *,
        tool_id: UUID,
        version: str,
    ) -> ToolVersion | None:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(ToolVersion)
            .where(
                ToolVersion.tool_id == tool_id,
                ToolVersion.version == version,
            )
        )

        return result.scalar_one_or_none()

    async def get_active(
        self,
        *,
        tool_id: UUID,
    ) -> ToolVersion | None:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(ToolVersion)
            .where(
                ToolVersion.tool_id == tool_id,
                ToolVersion.status
                == ToolVersionStatus.ACTIVE,
                ToolVersion.enabled.is_(True),
            )
            .order_by(
                ToolVersion.created_at.desc()
            )
        )

        return result.scalars().first()

    async def list_versions(
        self,
        *,
        tool_id: UUID,
    ) -> list[ToolVersion]:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(ToolVersion)
            .where(
                ToolVersion.tool_id == tool_id
            )
            .order_by(
                ToolVersion.created_at.desc()
            )
        )

        return list(result.scalars().all())

from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from ..models.tool_capability import ToolCapability


class ToolCapabilityRepository:

    def __init__(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession,
    ) -> None:
        self.session = session

    async def list_for_tool(
        self,
        tool_id: UUID,
    ) -> list[ToolCapability]:

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(ToolCapability)
            .where(
                ToolCapability.tool_id == tool_id
            )
            .order_by(
                ToolCapability.capability
            )
        )

        return list(result.scalars().all())

    async def find_by_capability(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: UUID,
        capability: str,
    ) -> list[ToolCapability]:

        from ..models.tool import Tool

        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(ToolCapability)
            .join(Tool)
            .where(
                Tool.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                Tool.enabled.is_(True),
                ToolCapability.capability
                == capability,
            )
        )

        return list(result.scalars().all())

19. Domain ToolDefinition
Maintenant nous séparons complètement :
DATABASE MODEL
de :
RUNTIME DOMAIN OBJECT
C'est essentiel.
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable

from ..domain.enums import (
    PermissionLevel,
    ToolRisk,
)


ToolHandler = Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ToolDefinition:

    name: str
    version: str

    description: str

    handler: ToolHandler

    input_schema: dict[str, Any]
    output_schema: dict[str, Any]

    capabilities: frozenset[str]

    permissions: frozenset[PermissionLevel]

    risk_level: ToolRisk

    timeout_seconds: int

    max_retries: int = 0

    requires_sandbox: bool = True

    requires_approval: bool = False

    enabled: bool = True

    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(
        default_factory=dict
    )

20. Registry DB
Voici le composant qui transforme PostgreSQL en Registry runtime.
from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from ..domain.enums import PermissionLevel
from ..domain.tool_definition import ToolDefinition
from ..models.tool import Tool
from ..repositories.tool_repository import ToolRepository
from ..repositories.tool_version_repository import (
    ToolVersionRepository,
)
from ..repositories.tool_capability_repository import (
    ToolCapabilityRepository,
)
from ..repositories.tool_permission_repository import (
    ToolPermissionRepository,
)


class ToolRegistryDB:

    def __init__(
        self,
        tool_repository: ToolRepository,
        version_repository: ToolVersionRepository,
        capability_repository: ToolCapabilityRepository,
        permission_repository: ToolPermissionRepository,
        handler_resolver,
    ) -> None:

        self.tools = tool_repository
        self.versions = version_repository
        self.capabilities = capability_repository
        self.permissions = permission_repository

        self.handler_resolver = handler_resolver

    async def resolve(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: UUID,
        name: str,
        version: str | None = None,
    ) -> ToolDefinition:

        tool = await self.tools.get_by_name(
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            name=name,
        )

        if tool is None:
            raise LookupError(
                f"Tool not found: {name}"
            )

        if not tool.enabled:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Tool disabled: {name}"
            )

        if version:

            tool_version = (
                await self.versions.get_version(
                    tool_id=tool.id,
                    version=version,
                )
            )

        else:

            tool_version = (
                await self.versions.get_active(
                    tool_id=tool.id,
                )
            )

        if tool_version is None:
            raise LookupError(
                f"No active version for tool: {name}"
            )

        capabilities = (
            await self.capabilities.list_for_tool(
                tool.id
            )
        )

        permissions = (
            await self.permissions.list_for_tool(
                tool.id
            )
        )

        handler = self.handler_resolver.resolve(
            tool_version.implementation
        )

        return ToolDefinition(
            name=tool.name,
            version=tool_version.version,
            description=tool.description,
            handler=handler,
            input_schema=tool.input_schema,
            output_schema=tool.output_schema,
            capabilities=frozenset(
                c.capability
                for c in capabilities
            ),
            permissions=frozenset(
                p.permission
                for p in permissions
                if p.allowed
            ),
            risk_level=tool.risk_level,
            timeout_seconds=tool.timeout_seconds,
            requires_approval=any(
                p.requires_approval
                for p in permissions
                if p.allowed
            ),
            enabled=tool.enabled,
            metadata={
                **tool.metadata_,
                **tool_version.metadata_,
            },
        )

21. Capability Discovery
Le Registry doit également permettre :
async def discover_by_capability(
    self,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    capability: str,
) -> list[ToolDefinition]:
Implémentation :
async def discover_by_capability(
    self,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    capability: str,
) -> list[ToolDefinition]:

    rows = await self.capabilities.find_by_capability(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        capability=capability,
    )

    result = []

    for capability_row in rows:

        tool = await self.tools.get(
            capability_row.tool_id
        )

        if tool is None or not tool.enabled:
            continue

        definition = await self.resolve(
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            name=tool.name,
        )

        result.append(definition)

    return result

22. Secure Handler Resolver
Il ne faut surtout pas permettre :
PostgreSQL
    ↓
importlib.import_module(
    valeur quelconque
)
Nous créons donc une allowlist.
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib


class SecureHandlerResolver:

    ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset({
        "yahria.execution.adapters.filesystem",
        "yahria.execution.adapters.terminal",
        "yahria.execution.adapters.git",
        "yahria.execution.adapters.search",
        "yahria.execution.adapters.tests",
        "yahria.execution.adapters.browser",
    })

    def resolve(self, path: str):

        module_name, function_name = path.split(
            ":",
            1,
        )

        if module_name not in self.ALLOWED_MODULES:
            raise PermissionError(
                f"Unauthorized tool module: "
                f"{module_name}"
            )

        module = importlib.import_module(
            module_name
        )

        handler = getattr(
            module,
            function_name,
            None,
        )

        if handler is None:
            raise LookupError(
                f"Handler not found: {path}"
            )

        if not callable(handler):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Handler is not callable: {path}"
            )

        return handler

25. Outils critiques
Les outils suivants ne doivent pas être activés par défaut :
CRITICAL_TOOLS = {
    "git.push",
    "production.deploy",
    "database.migrate.production",
    "secret.read",
}
Le seed doit les créer éventuellement comme :
enabled = false
risk = critical
requires_approval = true
Cela permet au Registry de les connaître sans leur permettre de s'exécuter.

26. Repository Transaction Boundary
Une règle importante :
Repository
    ↓
flush()
mais :
Service
    ↓
commit()
Les repositories ne doivent pas faire :
await session.commit()
Cela permet de composer plusieurs opérations dans une seule transaction.
Exemple :
Create Tool
    +
Create Version
    +
Create Capabilities
    +
Create Permissions
    ↓
ONE TRANSACTION
    ↓
COMMIT

27. Service de registration
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from ..models.tool import Tool
from ..models.tool_version import ToolVersion
from ..models.tool_capability import ToolCapability
from ..models.tool_permission import ToolPermission


class ToolRegistrationService:

    def __init__(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession,
        tool_repository,
    ):
        self.session = session
        self.tools = tool_repository

    async def register(
        self,
        *,
        tool: Tool,
        version: ToolVersion,
        capabilities: list[str],
        permissions: list[tuple],
    ) -> Tool:

        existing = await self.tools.get_by_name(
            tenant_id=tool.tenant_id,
            name=tool.name,
        )

        if existing is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Tool already exists: {tool.name}"
            )

        tool.versions.append(version)

        for capability in capabilities:

            tool.capabilities.append(
                ToolCapability(
                    capability=capability,
                )
            )

        for permission, requires_approval in permissions:

            tool.permissions.append(
                ToolPermission(
                    permission=permission,
                    allowed=True,
                    requires_approval=requires_approval,
                )
            )

        self.session.add(tool)

        await self.session.flush()

        return tool

28. AsyncSession Factory
Dans YAHRIA :
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
    AsyncSession,
    async_sessionmaker,
    create_async_engine,
)


engine = create_async_engine(
    DATABASE_URL,
    pool_pre_ping=True,
    pool_recycle=1800,
)

AsyncSessionFactory = async_sessionmaker(
    engine,
    class_=AsyncSession,
    expire_on_commit=False,
)

29. Tenant Isolation
D.3.1-A conserve la règle D.2 :
EVERY TENANT-OWNED TOOL QUERY
        ↓
tenant_id
Par exemple :
.where(
    Tool.tenant_id == tenant_id,
    Tool.name == name,
)
Mais il faut aller plus loin avec PostgreSQL RLS.
Le Repository n'est donc pas la sécurité ultime.
La défense est :
Application tenant filtering
+
PostgreSQL RLS

30. Architecture de sécurité
                    ToolRequest
                         │
                         ▼
                 tenant_id context
                         │
              ┌──────────┴──────────┐
              ▼                     ▼
        SQLAlchemy filter          RLS
              │                     │
              └──────────┬──────────┘
                         ▼
                    PostgreSQL
Ainsi une erreur applicative de type :
select(Tool)
ne doit pas permettre à un tenant de voir les outils d'un autre tenant.

    tools = await registry.discover_by_capability(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        capability="filesystem.read",
    )

    assert any(
        tool.name == "filesystem.read"
        for tool in tools
    )

5. Principe du Runtime Registry
Le registre runtime ne doit jamais être la source de vérité persistante.
PostgreSQL = source of truth
Runtime Registry = projection mémoire
Donc :
PostgreSQL
     │
     │ LOAD
     ▼
Runtime Registry
     │
     │ EXECUTION REQUEST
     ▼
ToolDefinition
Si PostgreSQL dit :
enabled = false
le runtime doit retirer le Tool.

8. Handler Resolver sécurisé
C'est une partie critique.
La DB contient par exemple :
yahria.execution.adapters.filesystem:read_file
Mais nous ne devons surtout pas permettre :
os.system
subprocess.run
malicious.module:handler
depuis PostgreSQL.
Resolver
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
from collections.abc import Callable


class SecureHandlerResolver:

    ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset(
        {
            "yahria.execution.adapters.filesystem",
            "yahria.execution.adapters.terminal",
            "yahria.execution.adapters.git",
            "yahria.execution.adapters.search",
            "yahria.execution.adapters.tests",
            "yahria.execution.adapters.browser",
        }
    )

    def resolve(self, path: str) -> Callable:

        if not path or ":" not in path:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid handler path: {path!r}"
            )

        module_name, function_name = path.split(":", 1)

        if module_name not in self.ALLOWED_MODULES:
            raise PermissionError(
                f"Handler module not allowed: {module_name}"
            )

        if not function_name:
            raise ValueError(
                "Handler function name cannot be empty"
            )

        module = importlib.import_module(module_name)

        handler = getattr(
            module,
            function_name,
            None,
        )

        if handler is None:
            raise LookupError(
                f"Handler not found: {path}"
            )

        if not callable(handler):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Handler is not callable: {path}"
            )

        return handler

9. Pourquoi cette protection est fondamentale
Sans allowlist :

     ▼
arbitrary Python

10. ToolLoader
Le Loader orchestre le chargement d'un Tool.
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from uuid import UUID

from yahria.execution.domain.tool_definition import ToolDefinition
from yahria.execution.registry.registry_entry import RegistryEntry


class ToolLoader:

    def __init__(
        self,
        registry_db,
        handler_resolver,
    ):
        self.registry_db = registry_db
        self.handler_resolver = handler_resolver

    async def load(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: UUID,
        name: str,
        version: str | None = None,
    ) -> RegistryEntry:

        definition = await self.registry_db.resolve(
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            name=name,
            version=version,
        )

        handler = self.handler_resolver.resolve(
            definition.metadata["implementation"]
        )

        runtime_definition = ToolDefinition(
            name=definition.name,
            version=definition.version,
            description=definition.description,
            handler=handler,
            input_schema=definition.input_schema,
            output_schema=definition.output_schema,
            capabilities=definition.capabilities,
            permissions=definition.permissions,
            risk_level=definition.risk_level,
            timeout_seconds=definition.timeout_seconds,
            max_retries=definition.max_retries,
            requires_sandbox=definition.requires_sandbox,
            requires_approval=definition.requires_approval,
            enabled=definition.enabled,
            metadata=definition.metadata,
        )

        return RegistryEntry(
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            definition=runtime_definition,
            loaded_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )
Mais une amélioration est nécessaire
Dans D.3.1-A, ToolDefinition ne contient pas directement implementation.
Je recommande donc de ne pas faire dépendre le runtime de metadata["implementation"].
Nous devons plutôt enrichir le contrat interne du Loader avec une structure explicite.

12. Runtime Registry
C'est le cœur de B.
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from uuid import UUID

from yahria.execution.registry.registry_entry import RegistryEntry
from yahria.execution.registry.registry_errors import (
    ToolNotFoundError,
    ToolRegistrationConflictError,
)


class RuntimeToolRegistry:

    def __init__(self):
        self._tools: dict[
            tuple[UUID, str, str],
            RegistryEntry,
        ] = {}

        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def register(
        self,
        entry: RegistryEntry,
    ) -> None:

        key = entry.key

        async with self._lock:

            if key in self._tools:
                raise ToolRegistrationConflictError(
                    f"Tool already registered: {key}"
                )

            self._tools[key] = entry

    async def replace(
        self,
        entry: RegistryEntry,
    ) -> None:

        async with self._lock:
            self._tools[entry.key] = entry

    async def unregister(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: UUID,
        name: str,
        version: str,
    ) -> None:

        key = (
            tenant_id,
            name,
            version,
        )

        async with self._lock:
            self._tools.pop(key, None)

    async def resolve(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id: UUID,
        name: str,
        version: str,
    ) -> RegistryEntry:

        key = (
            tenant_id,
            name,
            version,
        )

        entry = self._tools.get(key)

        if entry is None:
            raise ToolNotFoundError(
                f"Tool not registered: {name}@{version}"
            )

        return entry

13. Résolution de version active
Le runtime doit aussi permettre :
resolve_active(
    tenant_id,
    "filesystem.read",
)
async def resolve_active(
    self,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    name: str,
) -> RegistryEntry:

    candidates = [
        entry
        for key, entry in self._tools.items()
        if key[0] == tenant_id
        and key[1] == name
        and entry.definition.enabled
    ]

    if not candidates:
        raise ToolNotFoundError(name)

    candidates.sort(
        key=lambda item: item.definition.version,
        reverse=True,
    )

    return candidates[0]

Le tri lexical :
1.9.0

est incorrect.
Pour production, il faut utiliser un parseur SemVer.

17. Chargement global
Le Registry doit pouvoir initialiser YAHRIA.
class ToolRegistryBootstrap:

    def __init__(
        self,
        tool_repository,
        loader,
        runtime_registry,
    ):
        self.tool_repository = tool_repository
        self.loader = loader
        self.runtime_registry = runtime_registry

    async def load_tenant(
        self,
        tenant_id,
    ) -> int:

        tools = await self.tool_repository.list_enabled(
            tenant_id
        )

        loaded = 0

        for tool in tools:

            entry = await self.loader.load(
                tenant_id=tenant_id,
                name=tool.name,
            )

            await self.runtime_registry.replace(
                entry
            )

            loaded += 1

        return loaded

class RuntimeRegistryManager:

    def __init__(
        self,
        loader,
        registry,
    ):
        self.loader = loader
        self.registry = registry

    async def load(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id,
        name,
        version=None,
    ):

        entry = await self.loader.load(
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            name=name,
            version=version,
        )

        await self.registry.replace(entry)

        return entry

20. Hot Reload
YAHRIA doit pouvoir modifier un Tool sans redémarrer toute l'application.
Flux :
DB CHANGE
   ↓
INVALIDATION EVENT
   ↓
Registry Manager
   ↓
UNLOAD OLD
   ↓
LOAD NEW
   ↓
VALIDATE
   ↓
REGISTER
Exemple :
async def reload(
    self,
    *,
    tenant_id,
    name,
    version=None,
):

    entry = await self.loader.load(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        name=name,
        version=version,
    )

    await self.registry.replace(entry)

    return entry

21. Important : Reload atomique
Il ne faut jamais faire :
DELETE OLD
   ↓
LOAD NEW
car pendant quelques millisecondes le Tool disparaît.
Préférer :
LOAD NEW
   ↓
VALIDATE NEW
   ↓
REGISTER NEW
   ↓
REMOVE OLD
Ou mieux :
                Runtime Registry
                      │
             ┌────────┴────────┐
             │ Atomic Snapshot │
             └────────┬────────┘
                      │
          ┌───────────┴───────────┐
          ▼                       ▼
       Snapshot N             Snapshot N+1

23. Version finale du Runtime Registry
Je recommande donc cette architecture plutôt qu'un simple dict.
class RuntimeToolRegistry:

    def __init__(self):
        self._generation = 0
        self._tools = {}
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    @property
    def generation(self) -> int:
        return self._generation

    async def register(
        self,
        entry: RegistryEntry,
    ):

        async with self._lock:

            new_tools = dict(self._tools)

            new_tools[entry.key] = entry

            self._tools = new_tools
            self._generation += 1

    async def unregister(
        self,
        *,
        tenant_id,
        name,
        version,
    ):

        key = (
            tenant_id,
            name,
            version,
        )

        async with self._lock:

            if key not in self._tools:
                return

            new_tools = dict(self._tools)
            del new_tools[key]

            self._tools = new_tools
            self._generation += 1
C'est beaucoup plus sûr pour un runtime concurrent.

24. Health Check
D.3.1-B doit aussi savoir si le registre est sain.
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RegistryHealth:

    healthy: bool
    generation: int
    tool_count: int
    broken_tools: int
    errors: tuple[str, ...]
Service :
async def health(self) -> RegistryHealth:

    errors = []

    for entry in self._tools.values():

        if not entry.definition.enabled:
            continue

        if entry.definition.handler is None:
            errors.append(
                f"Missing handler: "
                f"{entry.definition.name}"
            )

    return RegistryHealth(
        healthy=not errors,
        generation=self._generation,
        tool_count=len(self._tools),
        broken_tools=len(errors),
        errors=tuple(errors),
    )

Avant registration :
ToolDefinition
       │
       ▼
┌───────────────────────────┐
│ Name valid?               │
│ Version valid?            │
│ Schema present?           │
│ Handler callable?         │
│ Timeout > 0?              │
│ Capabilities valid?       │
│ Permissions valid?        │
│ Risk valid?               │

Validator :
class ToolDefinitionLoaderValidator:

    def validate(
        self,
        definition: ToolDefinition,
    ) -> None:

        if not definition.name:
            raise ValueError("Tool name is required")

        if not definition.version:
            raise ValueError(
                "Tool version is required"
            )

        if definition.timeout_seconds <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "Timeout must be positive"
            )

        if not definition.input_schema:
            raise ValueError(
                "Input schema is required"
            )

        if not definition.output_schema:
            raise ValueError(
                "Output schema is required"
            )

        if not definition.permissions:
            raise ValueError(
                "Tool must have permissions"
            )

        if not callable(definition.handler):
            raise ValueError(
                "Tool handler is not callable"
            )
Le C développera cette validation beaucoup plus profondément.

31. Isolation multi-tenant
C'est absolument essentiel pour YAHRIA SaaS.
Interdit :
registry.resolve(
    name="filesystem.read"
)
sans tenant.
Obligatoire :
registry.resolve(
    tenant_id=tenant_id,
    name="filesystem.read",
    version="1.0.0",
)
Le cache doit donc être :
(tenant_id, tool_name, version)
et jamais :
(tool_name, version)

D.3.1-B est donc la couche qui transforme le Tool Registry persistant de D.3.1-A en un véritable registre d'outils utilisable par le moteur agentique YAHRIA, tout en conservant PostgreSQL comme source de vérité et sans donner à l'agent un accès direct au système.
La prochaine pièce logique est V2.2.2-D.3.1-C — VALIDATOR + CAPABILITY ENGINE, où l'on pourra notamment introduire le JSON Schema validator, capability matching, argument validation, compatibility checks, tool contract validation et capability graph, avant de laisser D.3.1-D prendre la décision d'autorisation.

V2.2.2-D.3.1-C — VALIDATOR + CAPABILITY ENGINE
Nous arrivons à la couche qui doit empêcher qu'un Tool mal formé, incompatible ou surdimensionné atteigne le moteur d'autorisation.

L'objectif de C n'est pas de décider si l'agent est autorisé à utiliser le Tool. C'est D.3.1-D.
C décide :
« Cette requête est-elle techniquement et contractuellement valide, et le Tool possède-t-il les capacités nécessaires ? »

4. Deux types de validation

A. Validation du Tool

       ↓

Le Tool lui-même est-il correctement défini ?

5. ValidationResult
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ValidationIssue:
    code: str
    message: str
    path: str | None = None
    severity: str = "error"
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(
        default_factory=dict
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ValidationResult:
    valid: bool
    issues: tuple[ValidationIssue, ...] = ()

    @property
    def errors(self) -> tuple[ValidationIssue, ...]:
        return tuple(
            issue
            for issue in self.issues
            if issue.severity == "error"
        )

    @property
    def warnings(self) -> tuple[ValidationIssue, ...]:
        return tuple(
            issue
            for issue in self.issues
            if issue.severity == "warning"
        )
Cela évite de simplement retourner :
True
False
YAHRIA doit savoir pourquoi une validation échoue.

7. JSON Schema Validator
Le contrat :
ToolDefinition.input_schema
définit ce que l'outil accepte.
Exemple :
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["path"],
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "encoding": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "utf-8"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
Puis :
ToolRequest.arguments
       ↓
JSON Schema
       ↓
VALID / INVALID

8. Implémentation
Je recommande jsonschema pour cette couche.
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator


class SchemaValidator:

    def validate(
        self,
        *,
        schema: dict,
        data: dict,
    ) -> ValidationResult:

        validator = Draft202012Validator(schema)

        issues = []

        for error in validator.iter_errors(data):

            path = ".".join(
                str(part)
                for part in error.absolute_path
            )

            issues.append(
                ValidationIssue(
                    code="invalid_arguments",
                    message=error.message,
                    path=path or None,
                )
            )

        return ValidationResult(
            valid=not issues,
            issues=tuple(issues),
        )

9. Pourquoi Draft 2020-12
Pour YAHRIA, je recommande de standardiser sur :
JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
Cela permet notamment :
    • type 
    • required 
    • properties 
    • additionalProperties 
    • enum 
    • const 
    • pattern 
    • minimum 
    • maximum 
    • items 
    • oneOf 
    • anyOf 
    • allOf 
    • $ref 

10. Protection contre les schémas dangereux
Le Validator ne doit pas accepter aveuglément n'importe quel schéma venant de PostgreSQL.
Il faut vérifier :
Schema
 │
 ├── valid JSON?
 ├── valid JSON Schema?
 ├── depth limit?
 ├── size limit?
 ├── recursive reference?
 ├── unsupported keyword?
 └── valid?
Exemple :
MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES = 256_000
MAX_SCHEMA_DEPTH = 32

11. DefinitionValidator
class DefinitionValidator:

    def __init__(
        self,
        schema_validator: SchemaValidator,
    ):
        self.schema_validator = schema_validator

    def validate(
        self,
        definition,
    ) -> ValidationResult:

        issues = []

        if not definition.name:
            issues.append(
                ValidationIssue(
                    code="invalid_contract",
                    message="Tool name is required",
                )
            )

        if not definition.version:
            issues.append(
                ValidationIssue(
                    code="invalid_version",
                    message="Tool version is required",
                )
            )

        if definition.timeout_seconds <= 0:
            issues.append(
                ValidationIssue(
                    code="invalid_contract",
                    message="Timeout must be positive",
                )
            )

        if not definition.permissions:
            issues.append(
                ValidationIssue(
                    code="invalid_contract",
                    message="Tool has no permissions",
                )
            )

        if not callable(definition.handler):
            issues.append(
                ValidationIssue(
                    code="handler_invalid",
                    message="Handler is not callable",
                )
            )

        input_result = self.schema_validator.validate(
            schema=definition.input_schema,
            data={},
        )

        # Ici, on ne valide pas réellement les arguments.
        # On valide d'abord la structure du schema.

        return ValidationResult(
            valid=not issues,
            issues=tuple(issues),
        )
Dans la version industrielle, la validation du schema lui-même sera séparée de celle des arguments.

12. RequestValidator
class RequestValidator:

    def __init__(
        self,
        schema_validator: SchemaValidator,
    ):
        self.schema_validator = schema_validator

    def validate(
        self,
        *,
        request,
        tool,
    ) -> ValidationResult:

        if not tool.enabled:

            return ValidationResult(
                valid=False,
                issues=(
                    ValidationIssue(
                        code="tool_disabled",
                        message=(
                            f"Tool disabled: "
                            f"{tool.name}"
                        ),
                    ),
                ),
            )

        return self.schema_validator.validate(
            schema=tool.input_schema,
            data=request.arguments,
        )

class CapabilityMatcher:

    def match(
        self,
        *,
        provided: frozenset[str],
        required: frozenset[str],
    ) -> CapabilityMatchResult:

        missing = required - provided

        matched = not missing

        score = (
            1.0
            if matched
            else len(
                required - missing
            ) / max(len(required), 1)
        )

        return CapabilityMatchResult(
            matched=matched,
            required=required,
            provided=provided,
            missing=frozenset(missing),
            conflicts=frozenset(),
            dependencies_missing=frozenset(),
            score=score,
        )

class CapabilityGraph:

    def __init__(self):
        self._nodes: dict[
            str,
            CapabilityDefinition
        ] = {}

    def register(
        self,
        capability: CapabilityDefinition,
    ):
        self._nodes[capability.name] = capability

    def get(
        self,
        name: str,
    ) -> CapabilityDefinition | None:
        return self._nodes.get(name)

22. Expansion des capacités
Exemple :
Tool provides:

Le moteur peut calculer :

C'est une distinction critique pour la sécurité.

23. Capability Closure
class CapabilityExpander:

    def __init__(self, graph):
        self.graph = graph

    def expand(
        self,
        capabilities: frozenset[str],
    ) -> frozenset[str]:

        result = set(capabilities)

        changed = True

        while changed:

            changed = False

            for name in list(result):

                definition = self.graph.get(name)

                if not definition:
                    continue

                parents = set()

                if definition.parent:
                    parents.add(
                        definition.parent
                    )

                parents.update(
                    definition.implies
                )

                for parent in parents:

                    if parent not in result:
                        result.add(parent)
                        changed = True

        return frozenset(result)

27. Capability Engine complet
class CapabilityEngine:

    def __init__(
        self,
        graph: CapabilityGraph,
    ):
        self.graph = graph
        self.expander = CapabilityExpander(graph)
        self.matcher = CapabilityMatcher()

    def evaluate(
        self,
        *,
        provided: frozenset[str],
        required: frozenset[str],
    ) -> CapabilityMatchResult:

        expanded = self.expander.expand(
            provided
        )

        result = self.matcher.match(
            provided=expanded,
            required=required,
        )

        return result

Tool B = partial

32. Validation Pipeline complet
class ToolRequestValidationPipeline:

    async def validate(
        self,
        *,
        request,
        tool,
        requirements,
    ):

        definition_result = (
            self.definition_validator.validate(tool)
        )

        if not definition_result.valid:
            return definition_result

        request_result = (
            self.request_validator.validate(
                request=request,
                tool=tool,
            )
        )

        if not request_result.valid:
            return request_result

        capability_result = (
            self.capability_engine.evaluate(
                provided=tool.capabilities,
                required=requirements.capabilities,
            )
        )

        if not capability_result.matched:
            return ValidationResult(
                valid=False,
                issues=tuple(
                    ValidationIssue(
                        code="capability_missing",
                        message=(
                            f"Missing capabilities: "
                            f"{sorted(capability_result.missing)}"
                        ),
                    ),
                ),
            )

        return ValidationResult(
            valid=True
        )

34. Ce que C interdit
Exemple :
Agent
 ↓
filesystem.read
 ↓
arguments = {
    "path": "../../etc/passwd"
}
Le JSON Schema peut être valide.
Mais C ne doit pas prétendre que la requête est totalement sûre.
Pourquoi ?
Parce que :
"path": "../../etc/passwd"
relève de la policy/path security, qui appartient à D.3.1-D et D.4.
Donc :
C = contract validity
D = authorization/security
D.4 = isolation
Cette séparation est très importante.

35. C ne doit pas devenir un deuxième Policy Engine
C
Est-ce techniquement valide ?
Possède-t-il la capacité ?
D
Est-il autorisé ?
Quel est le risque ?
Faut-il une approbation ?
D.4
Dans quel sandbox ?
Quels chemins ?
Quel réseau ?
Quelles ressources ?

Point architectural particulièrement important
Avec D.3.1-C, YAHRIA possède maintenant trois niveaux de contrôle clairement séparés :
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ C — VALIDATION                             │
│ "La requête est-elle techniquement valide?"│
└─────────────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                      ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ D — AUTHORIZATION                          │
│ "Est-elle autorisée et quel est son risque?"│
└─────────────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                      ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ D.4 — ISOLATION                            │
│ "Dans quel environnement peut-elle tourner?"│
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
C'est cette séparation qui empêchera YAHRIA de devenir un simple agent LLM capable d'appeler arbitrairement Python.
La prochaine étape logique est donc V2.2.2-D.3.1-D — PERMISSION + RISK + APPROVAL ENGINE : on prendra le ValidationResult et le CapabilityMatchResult de C pour construire le véritable Policy Decision Point (PDP) de YAHRIA, avec matrice RBAC/ABAC, niveaux de risque, règles par tenant/projet/workspace, approbation humaine, expiration des autorisations et décision ALLOW / DENY / REQUIRE_APPROVAL.
V2.2.2-D.3.1-D 



V2.2.2-D.3.1-D — PERMISSION + RISK + APPROVAL ENGINE
Nous passons maintenant de « le Tool est valide et possède la capacité » à :
« YAHRIA autorise-t-il réellement cette action, dans ce contexte, avec ce niveau de risque, et faut-il demander une approbation humaine ? »
C'est le Policy Decision Point (PDP) du Tool Runtime.

6. AuthorizationDecision
Le contrat D.3.1-D :
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from enum import StrEnum


class AuthorizationEffect(StrEnum):
    ALLOW = "allow"
    DENY = "deny"
    REQUIRE_APPROVAL = "require_approval"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AuthorizationDecision:

    effect: AuthorizationEffect

    allowed: bool

    requires_approval: bool

    risk_score: float

    risk_level: str

    permissions: frozenset

    reasons: tuple[str, ...]

    policy_name: str

    expires_at: datetime | None = None

    metadata: dict = field(
        default_factory=dict

7. Important : trois états, pas deux
Une mauvaise architecture ferait :
ALLOW
DENY
YAHRIA doit avoir :
ALLOW
DENY
REQUIRE_APPROVAL
Exemple :
git.status
    → ALLOW

git.push
    → REQUIRE_APPROVAL

production.deploy
    → REQUIRE_APPROVAL / DENY

    → DENY

Les permissions D.2 sont :

Le Tool déclare :

9. Permission Resolver
class PermissionResolver:

    def resolve(
        self,
        *,
        tool_permissions: frozenset,
        allowed_permissions: frozenset,
    ) -> frozenset:

        return (
            tool_permissions
            & allowed_permissions
        )
Mais l'intersection seule n'est pas suffisante.

10. Permission Engine
class PermissionEngine:

    def evaluate(
        self,
        *,
        required: frozenset,
        allowed: frozenset,
    ) -> tuple[bool, frozenset]:

        missing = required - allowed

        return (
            not missing,
            frozenset(missing),
        )

11. Hiérarchie des permissions
Je recommande de ne pas considérer :
ADMIN > tout
comme une simple hiérarchie implicite.
Il vaut mieux utiliser des règles explicites.
Par exemple :
ADMIN
 ├── configuration
 ├── policy
 ├── secret-management
 └── deployment
et non :
ADMIN = READ + WRITE + EXECUTE + NETWORK + GIT
Cela évite une escalade involontaire.

Le Policy Engine est le véritable moteur RBAC + ABAC de D.

Subject

Context
Environment
C'est le modèle S-R-A-C-E :
SUBJECT
RESOURCE
ACTION
CONTEXT
ENVIRONMENT

20. Ordre de priorité
Il faut éviter les conflits :
DENY
  >
REQUIRE_APPROVAL
  >
ALLOW
mais avec une règle encore plus forte :
Une règle explicite de blocage critique ne peut jamais être annulée par une simple règle ALLOW.
Donc :
CRITICAL DENY
      ↓
final = DENY

21. Policy Matcher
class PolicyMatcher:

    def matches(
        self,
        rule: PolicyRule,
        context: PolicyContext,
    ) -> bool:

        if not rule.enabled:
            return False

        # Implémentation réelle :
        # DSL / JSON conditions / operators.

        return self._evaluate_conditions(
            rule.conditions,
            context,
        )

22. Ne pas utiliser eval()
Absolument interdit :
eval(policy.expression)
Une policy ne doit jamais exécuter du Python arbitraire.
Utiliser un DSL déclaratif :
{
  "all": [
    {
      "field": "action.tool_name",
      "operator": "equals",
      "value": "git.push"
    },
    {
      "field": "environment.production",
      "operator": "equals",
      "value": true
    }
  ]
}

Et :

24. Risk Engine
Maintenant la question :
Même si le Tool est autorisé, quel est son risque ?
Le risque doit être calculé à partir de plusieurs facteurs.
Risk
├── Tool risk
├── Permission risk
├── Resource risk
├── Environment risk
├── Path risk
├── Network risk
├── Data sensitivity
├── Blast radius
├── Reversibility
└── Historical risk

25. RiskFactor
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RiskFactor:

    name: str

    score: float

    weight: float

    reason: str
Score :
0.0 → 1.0

26. Risk Score
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RiskScore:

    score: float

    factors: tuple[RiskFactor, ...]

    level: str
Classification :
0.00 – 0.24 → LOW
0.25 – 0.49 → MEDIUM
0.50 – 0.74 → HIGH
0.75 – 1.00 → CRITICAL

27. Risk Engine
class RiskEngine:

    def calculate(
        self,
        context: AuthorizationContext,
        tool,
    ) -> RiskScore:

        factors = []

        factors.append(
            RiskFactor(
                name="tool_risk",
                score=self._tool_score(
                    tool.risk_level
                ),
                weight=0.25,
                reason="Tool intrinsic risk",
            )
        )

        factors.append(
            RiskFactor(
                name="environment",
                score=self._environment_score(
                    context
                ),
                weight=0.25,
                reason="Execution environment",
            )
        )

        factors.append(
            RiskFactor(
                name="permission",
                score=self._permission_score(
                    tool.permissions
                ),
                weight=0.20,
                reason="Required permissions",
            )
        )

        factors.append(
            RiskFactor(
                name="blast_radius",
                score=self._blast_radius(
                    context
                ),
                weight=0.20,
                reason="Potential impact",
            )
        )

        factors.append(
            RiskFactor(
                name="reversibility",
                score=self._reversibility(
                    context
                ),
                weight=0.10,
                reason="Action reversibility",
            )
        )

        score = sum(
            f.score * f.weight
            for f in factors
        )

        return RiskScore(
            score=min(max(score, 0.0), 1.0),
            factors=tuple(factors),
            level=self._classify(score),
        )

28. Exemple de scoring
filesystem.read
Tool risk       0.05
Environment     0.05
Permission      0.05
Blast radius    0.05
Reversibility   0.00
Résultat :
LOW
filesystem.delete
Tool risk       0.60
Environment     0.30
Permission      0.70
Blast radius    0.80
Reversibility   0.90
Résultat :
HIGH / CRITICAL

29. Risk ne remplace pas Policy
Très important :
LOW risk
ne signifie pas automatiquement :
ALLOW
Exemple :
secret.read
risk = LOW
peut malgré tout être :
DENY
par policy.
Donc :
Risk ≠ Authorization

30. Approval Engine
L'Approval Engine intervient lorsque :
policy = REQUIRE_APPROVAL
ou :
risk >= approval_threshold
ou une règle spécifique l'impose.

31. Approval Request
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ApprovalRequest:

    execution_id: UUID

    tool_call_id: UUID | None

    action: str

    risk_level: str

    risk_score: float

    reason: str

    requested_by: UUID | None

    expires_at: datetime

    metadata: dict = field(
        default_factory=dict
    )

32. Approval Engine
class ApprovalEngine:

    def requires_approval(
        self,
        *,
        risk_score: RiskScore,
        policy_effect: PolicyEffect,
        threshold: float,
    ) -> bool:

        if policy_effect == (
            PolicyEffect.REQUIRE_APPROVAL
        ):
            return True

        return risk_score.score >= threshold

33. Exemple
Policy :
git.push
→ REQUIRE_APPROVAL
Risk :
0.62
Résultat :
REQUIRE_APPROVAL
YAHRIA crée :
execution.approval_requests

34. Expiration
Une approbation ne doit jamais être éternelle.
APPROVAL
   │
   ├── created
   ├── pending
   ├── approved
   ├── denied
   └── expired
Exemple :
expires_at = now() + 10 minutes

35. Approval Binding
Une approbation doit être liée à l'action exacte.
Il ne faut pas :
"J'approuve git.push"
de manière générale.
Il faut approuver :
tenant
project
workspace
execution
tool
version
arguments hash
branch
commit
risk

36. Approval Fingerprint
Je recommande :
Approval Subject
      │
      ├── tool
      ├── version
      ├── arguments
      ├── workspace
      ├── branch
      ├── policy
      └── risk

Ainsi, si l'agent modifie les arguments après approbation :
hash_old != hash_new
L'approbation devient invalide.
C'est une protection extrêmement importante.

37. Authorization Engine
Tout est maintenant assemblé.
class AuthorizationEngine:

    def __init__(
        self,
        permission_engine,
        policy_engine,
        risk_engine,
        approval_engine,
    ):
        self.permission_engine = permission_engine
        self.policy_engine = policy_engine
        self.risk_engine = risk_engine
        self.approval_engine = approval_engine

38. Pipeline d'autorisation
async def authorize(
    self,
    *,
    context,
    tool,
    validation_result,
    capability_result,
):

    if not validation_result.valid:
        return self._deny(
            "Tool request validation failed"
        )

    if not capability_result.matched:
        return self._deny(
            "Required capability missing"
        )

    permission_ok, missing = (
        self.permission_engine.evaluate(
            required=tool.permissions,
            allowed=context.permissions,
        )
    )

    if not permission_ok:
        return self._deny(
            f"Missing permissions: {missing}"
        )

    policy_decision = (
        await self.policy_engine.evaluate(
            context
        )
    )

    if policy_decision.effect == (
        PolicyEffect.DENY
    ):
        return self._deny(
            policy_decision.reason
        )

    risk = self.risk_engine.calculate(
        context,
        tool,
    )

    requires_approval = (
        self.approval_engine.requires_approval(
            risk_score=risk,
            policy_effect=policy_decision.effect,
            threshold=0.50,
        )
    )

    if requires_approval:

        return AuthorizationDecision(
            effect=AuthorizationEffect.REQUIRE_APPROVAL,
            allowed=False,
            requires_approval=True,
            risk_score=risk.score,
            risk_level=risk.level,
            permissions=tool.permissions,
            reasons=(
                "Human approval required",
            ),
            policy_name=policy_decision.policy_name,
        )

    return AuthorizationDecision(
        effect=AuthorizationEffect.ALLOW,
        allowed=True,
        requires_approval=False,
        risk_score=risk.score,
        risk_level=risk.level,
        permissions=tool.permissions,
        reasons=(
            "Authorization granted",
        ),
        policy_name=policy_decision.policy_name,
    )

Parce que certaines actions doivent être non délégables.

42. Non-delegable actions
Je recommande d'introduire :
NON_DELEGABLE
pour :
secret.read
production.credentials
root.access
security.policy.disable
audit.delete
Cela signifie :
Human approval
     ≠
automatic permission
Certaines opérations restent interdites même après approbation standard.

43. Break-glass
Pour les environnements réellement industriels, on peut prévoir plus tard :
BREAK_GLASS
Mais avec :
    • double approbation ; 
    • durée extrêmement courte ; 
    • audit obligatoire ; 
    • justification ; 
    • notification ; 
    • journal immuable. 
Ce mécanisme ne doit pas être activé par défaut.

44. Contextual Policy
Une des forces de YAHRIA sera :
même Tool
+
même agent
≠
même autorisation

Workspace dev
ALLOW
Workspace staging
ALLOW + risk check
Workspace production
REQUIRE_APPROVAL
